extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of scientific method, philosophy of science, and history of science
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of Francis Bacon's taxonomy of 'instances' (types of observations/cases) and procedural guidance for collecting and using them in inductive scientific inquiry; includes definitions, uses, cautions, and examples for each instance-type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Deviantes (Deviating Instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors of nature, vagaries, and monsters: cases where nature declines and deflects from its ordinary course; contrasted with monodicae (species-miracles) since deviating instances are miracles of individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not stop inquiry until the cause of such deviation is discovered; these instances sharpen and vivify the inquiry, rectify the intellect against habit, and reveal latent processes rather than fixed forms. Compile a particular natural history of all monsters, rarities, and novelties, but with severe selection to ensure trustworthiness; be especially suspicious of reports tied to religion, magicians, alchemists, or other unreliable narrators. Examples/notes: discovery of Neptune from perturbations of Uranus; Saturn's rings and red eclipse flames cited as deviating instances in commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantiae Monodicae (Monodic Instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances described as 'miracles of species' (monodicae) — phenomena that are remarkable in relation to a species (not merely individuals) and that illuminate the form or nature of that species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monodicae help correct the intellect and reveal common forms; they are particularly effective in instructing practice and in disclosing general laws when their nature is explained. Examples referenced include singular natural exemplars such as the sun, moon, magnet, etc.; monodicae differ from deviating instances in being species-level marvels rather than individual anomalies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Limitaneas / Participia (Limiting / Partaking Instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances exhibiting bodies that seem composed of two species or intermediate between species; 'participia' that partake of two or more kinds and appear to stand between the singular and deviating instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat separately because they excellently indicate composition and fabrication of things and hint the causes of number and quality of ordinary species; examples include moss (questioned by commentators), certain comets (between stars and meteors), flying-fish (appearance between birds and fishes), bats (appearance between birds and quadrupeds), and the Dipnoi (lungfish) as a good zoological example. Use these to infer fabrication/compositional relations and to trace transitions between taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Potestatis / Fascimi (Instances of Power / Works of Art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances consisting of the most noble and perfect works of art (consummate productions in each art), i.e., human-made masterpieces and powerful artifices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study these 'instances of power' because they often indicate proximate routes to new inventions or applications: by attentively urging and extending these artifices one may produce new works, adapt them to nobler uses, or derive new methods. However, exercise caution: such masterpieces can overawe and fix the intellect (making one believe nothing else is possible except by the same method). Compile a particular history of masterworks together with their modes of effecting/operation. Include in the survey both mechanical and liberal arts, and pay attention to artificial monodicae (e.g., papyrus as an artificial substance imitating nature). Do not dismiss toys, prestidigitation, or even reputedly superstitious/magical practices — inspect them briefly for possible natural operations (sympathy, transmission of impressions, etc.). Examples: steam engine, electric telegraph, chloroform, photography; papyrus contrasted with textiles and concretes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Comitatus and Hostiles (Instances of Accompaniment / Hostile Instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete bodies in which the nature in question perpetually follows (comitatus) or is perpetually excluded (hostilis); such instances furnish universal affirmative or universal negative propositions about the nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to form universal propositions (affirmative or negative) and to 'narrow' or circumscribe the affirmative form. Attach to universal propositions those concrete instances that approach the limit between being and non-being (near-concretes) to indicate the boundaries of the form (e.g., weak flames or gold near incorruptibility). Universal propositions need not be absolutely exact — singular or rare exceptions may be tolerated but must always be explained. Examples: flame as comitatus for heat (every flame is hot); air as hostile to consistency (air cannot 'consist'). Caveat: reasoning based solely on hostile instances can be liable to error; qualifiers may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Subjunctivas / Ultimitatis sive Termini (Subjunctive / Ultimate Instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that by themselves and in their property indicate clear sections of nature, measures of things, and how far nature proceeds in an action — i.e., ultimate or terminal cases marking extremes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to determine limits and measures (the 'Quousque' of nature) and transitions to other states. Include both supreme and lowest grades of a property (e.g., gold in weight, iron in hardness, silk in softness, vermiculi cutis in quantity of animals, ignition of pyritic powder in rapid expansion). These instances are valuable in fixing the scale and extreme behavior of the nature under study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantias Foederis / Unionis (Instances of Alliance / Conjunction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that unite or confuse natures thought to be heterogeneous, showing that operations attributed to one nature may also occur in others — thus undermining supposed essential heterogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alliance instances to elevate the intellect from differences to genera and remove spurious divisions (larvae) among substances; they are especially powerful for discovering common explanations and building broader genera from apparent differences. Example: the fall of detached bodies suggesting a common explanation for terrestrial gravitation and celestial motions (Newton-like analogy). Another example in text: distinctions among three kinds of heat (celestial, animal, fire) and experiments showing overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instantiae Migrantibus (Instances of Migration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances in which a nature is mobile in concrete things — i.e., the property may come and go (accedens/recidens) or be acquired or deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instances are used to restrict and narrow the affirmative form: the form of the thing must account for the property being acquired or lost by migration. Particular propositions drawn from such migrating instances are less privileged unless they inform about migration; use them to detect accidental vs. essential properties and to refine hypotheses about form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect early and with severe selection; prefer reliable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The five (and other) special instance-types should not be reserved but collected from the start as part of a particular history; collection must be done with the severest selection so that faith/trust in reports is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble a 'congeries' or history of particular instances (monsters, rarities, artifices, etc.) early to correct and purge the intellect of habitual prejudices. Be especially suspicious of instances that rest on religious prodigies or the writings of magicians/alchemists; instead extract instances from grave and faithful histories and certain auditions. The collected instances prepare the mind to receive pure notions and pave the way for operative practice. Also prepare catalogues (e.g., Catalogus Historiarum Particularium) and histories of masterworks with methods of operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the absence of universal affirmatives/negatives as informative
rubrics_metrics.description: If a universal affirmative or universal negative cannot be established for a nature, that very absence should be carefully noted (regarded as a kind of non-being).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording the failure to attain a universal is itself valuable data — e.g., no universal hostile instance for 'calidum' (heat) in known bodies; inability to assert 'eternal' or 'incorruptible' of sublunary bodies should be recorded. Such absences indicate limits of current knowledge and require attention/possible explanation.
